0|79e68821582d08e369094e7ea45dbfb8fdb37d7e|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"ath10k: go back to using dma_alloc_coherent() for firmware scratch memory
This reverts commit b057886524be (""ath10k: do not use coherent memory for
allocated device memory chunks"") in 2015 which converted this allocation from
dma_map_coherent() to kzalloc() / dma_map_single().
The current problem manifests when using later model NICs with larger
(>700KiB) scratch spaces in memory.  Although the kzalloc call
succeeds
column2: the software IOMMU TLB code (via dma_map_single()) panics

column1: because it can't find 700KiB of linear physmem bounce buffers for DMA.
Now
column2: this is a bit of a silly failure mode for the dma map API

column1: but it's what we currently have to play with.
In these cases
call fails.
After chatting with Linus briefly about this
using dma_alloc_coherent() for doing larger device memory allocation
that requires some kind of physical address mapping.
You're not supposed to be using kzalloc and dma_map_* calls for
large memory regions
column2: and I'm guessing not for long-held mappings

column1: either.  Typically dma mappings should be temporary for DMA
not long held like these.
Now
column2: since hopefully the major annoying underlying problem has also been

column1: addressed (ie
column2: ath10k is no longer tears down all of these allocations

column1: and reallocates them every time the vdevs are brought down) fragmentation
should stop being such a touchy issue.  If it is though
dma_alloc_coherent() use gets us access to the CMB APIs too relatively
easily and ideally we would be allocating memory early in boot for
exactly these reasons.
